offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

Every recent payments-api error reads 'provider unavailable; payment left pending': /v1/payments was not sent because the circuit breaker is open.
Every service, the provider included, was created together at 20:45:50 with normal settings (PROVIDER_BREAKER on, CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT cents). No later deploy explains a change.
Provider calls returned HTTP 500 at a rising rate from 20:46:45 to 20:47:31, and successful 200 answers then fell to zero by 20:48:16.

POST /payments traces from 20:47:17 to 20:47:23 lasted 6.2 to 9.6 s.

One 9.6 s POST /payments made three POSTs to fake-provider /v1/payments, and each ended in an httpx ReadTimeout after about 3.0 s. The request then returned 503 and left the payment pending. The database and Redis spans took under 2 ms.

proposed_fix.summary: There is nothing to roll back on our side. Keep the breaker on, because it fails requests fast and protects payments-api. Escalate to the provider and watch for the breaker's trial calls to succeed. Once the provider recovers, reconcile the pending payments against the provider's records with money_check. Some payments that timed out may have been charged by the provider without us knowing, so confirm or retry them using the same idempotency keys, and do not create new payments for them.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Taking no action means new payments keep failing with 503 and stay pending until the provider recovers. Retrying pending payments later risks charging a customer twice if it is done without idempotency keys.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Nothing is changed, so there is nothing to undo. If the breaker's settings are tuned later, revert them to PROVIDER_BREAKER=on.

diagnosis.hypothesis: From about 20:46:45 the payment provider (fake-provider, outside) became unhealthy. After repeated failures the circuit breaker (PROVIDER_BREAKER=on) opened. Since about 20:48 payments-api rejects provider calls at once, leaves the payment pending and returns 503, which gives the 96% 5xx rate. The breaker is working as designed. All containers were created together at 20:45:50 with normal settings, so no regression is visible to roll back. Still open: why the provider is failing, whether it has recovered, and whether payments that timed out were charged by the provider. The c5 histogram appears to leave out timed-out calls.
